title: QA coverage: fail-closed answer engine, all checks green
headline_insight: The answer engine passes 87/87 regression-bank checks and honestly answers 36.6% of answerable questions -- refusals are the fail-closed design, not a defect.
what_it_means: Every one of 87 regression-bank checks passes (fail-closed statuses count as PASS), and on a 1,307-row coverage stress test the engine answers 36.62% of the questions it deems answerable and declines the rest. Every one of 125 edge-language questions was refused (ok_rate 0.0), which is exactly the intended behavior.
how_to_read: Coverage rate is answered-ok divided by expects-answer-true rows only; no_data / not_supported / ambiguous / refused categories are excluded from the denominator by design.
why_it_matters: A predictor that refuses edge and ROI questions and returns no_data when it lacks data is safer than one that always answers, and the green regression bank proves that behavior is stable.
caveat: The 36.6% figure counts only rows flagged expects_answer=true; a large share of real questions still resolve to no_data (560 of the 1,307 stress rows).
